title: How do you use Astra?
author: takshit2
selftext:
I guess we can all agree that Opus 5.5 nailed the game dev but I wanted to see if Astra can help with building your games.

I was building a monster capturing game and I wanted to use both Astra and Opus. I was thinking on the art design side, astra can be useful then Opus is the general game design and architecture.

comments.author: orellanaed
comments.body: We don't all agree. Opus 5.5 turned to the dark side didn't you hear?

replies.author: Ok-Investment4414
replies.body: sigh think its still aight , and how to use astra ... as a code reviewer , sol 6.1 mad cheap and can do deep code dives, have claude code trigger 6 sol or astra make a review file and code code then reads and repairs. also cc uses gpt 6 to make reference images to help with blender rendering.

replies.author: takshit2
replies.body: Ok so basically Sol/Astra as sub critic and image gen. Thank you!

replies.author: Ok-Investment4414
replies.body: yeah atm 5.5 is doing better generations but the loop i describes al runs in cc which makes it even better

replies.author: MechaLenin111
replies.body: I was thinking of jumping ship from Astra/Sol for Opus 5.5. It was supposed to be great, what happened to it?

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: I have Astra reviewing implementations 24/7 right now. I don't trust it to do the implementations itself, but it acts well as a foil to Opus. It's a way for me to make use of my Astra usage despite its capability decreasing so much since launch. It does make for a better visual/spatial reviewer than Opus still, too. Also I still use it for any mockup images I need.

comments.author: Tom_Baron
comments.body: Opus 5.5 is god tier. However i have a strange workflow, i actually have my repo plugged into gpt chat for context. If im looking at a gameplay element, the conversation starts in the gpt webapp. Ill talk in plain english and iterate over the design principles of what im trying to build, reviewing each iterarion in chat. This can go on for some time. Once an idea is fleshed out, gpt creates a prompt for claude which i run in plan mode. I then review the plan to ensure my vision is applied to the codebase. Finally claude executes the update. This is token efficient and Opus 5.5 can be working for hours without running out of usage on a cheap plan!

replies.author: takshit2
replies.body: This is a great tip! You use Sol 6.1 or Astra?

replies.author: Tom_Baron
replies.body: Sol 6.1, Terra would do too most likely. However, its an engaging process. I approach the conversation as if I'm discussing a design element to a colleague, pointing out when it misses things and feeding back when it gives a good or bad idea. Its not just a "Design my board geometry" prompt and thats it. Its a "I quite like the idea of a smaller cluster of players for x reason but we have to consider y if we do this, what can you see in the game design docs that might cause us an issue here? Scaling back weapon range might be of benefit".

comments.author: MidSerpent
comments.body:
I use Astra for adversarial review of design and code. It’s expensive and I don’t have the big ChatGPT account 

I find that there’s a lot of benefit in having a different high thinking model than the one what wrote the plan or code review the code.
